audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Paul's prayer for Israel, zeal, Messiah and Law, word near you, confession/trust, no distinction, beautiful feet, hearing, Israel hearing. Anti-Jewish misuse must be rejected.

verses.restored: Siblings, the goodwill of my heart and my prayer to the Divine for them is for salvation/healing.

familiar.text: Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.

modern.text: Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.

original.text: Ἀδελφοί, ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας καὶ ἡ ⸀δέησις πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ ⸀αὐτῶν εἰς σωτηρίαν.

verses.restored: For I bear witness to them that they have zeal for the Divine, but not according to full knowledge.

familiar.text: For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.

modern.text: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.

original.text: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς ὅτι ζῆλον θεοῦ ἔχουσιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ κατʼ ἐπίγνωσιν,

verses.restored: For not knowing the righteousness/justice of the Divine, and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to the righteousness/justice of the Divine.

familiar.text: For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.

modern.text: Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.

original.text: ἀγνοοῦντες γὰρ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ τὴν ⸀ἰδίαν ζητοῦντες στῆσαι, τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ὑπετάγησαν·

verses.restored: For Messiah is the aim/completion of Law into righteousness/justice for everyone trusting.

familiar.text: For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.

modern.text: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.

original.text: τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστὸς εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι.

verses.restored: For Moses writes concerning the righteousness/justice from Law: The human who does these things will live by them.

familiar.text: For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them.

modern.text: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”

original.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ γράφει ⸂ὅτι τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ ⸀τοῦ νόμου⸃ ὁ ⸀ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν ⸀αὐτῇ.

verses.restored: But the righteousness/justice from trust speaks this way: Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? that is, to bring Messiah down;

familiar.text: But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:)

modern.text: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down)

original.text: ἡ δὲ ἐκ πίστεως δικαιοσύνη οὕτως λέγει· Μὴ εἴπῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου· Τίς ἀναβήσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν καταγαγεῖν·

verses.restored: or, Who will descend into the abyss? that is, to bring Messiah up from the dead.

familiar.text: Or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)

modern.text: or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”

original.text: ἤ· Τίς καταβήσεται εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χριστὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναγαγεῖν.

verses.restored: But what does it say? The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart; this is the word of trust that we proclaim.

familiar.text: But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;

modern.text: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming:

original.text: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει; Ἐγγύς σου τὸ ῥῆμά ἐστιν, ἐν τῷ στόματί σου καὶ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τῆς πίστεως ὃ κηρύσσομεν.

verses.restored: Because if you confess with your mouth Lord Jesus and trust in your heart that the Divine raised him from the dead, you will be saved/healed.

familiar.text: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.

modern.text: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.

original.text: ὅτι ἐὰν ⸀ὁμολογήσῃς ἐν τῷ στόματί ⸀σου κύριον Ἰησοῦν, καὶ πιστεύσῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου ὅτι ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, σωθήσῃ·

verses.restored: For with the heart one trusts into righteousness/justice, and with the mouth one confesses into salvation/healing.

familiar.text: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

modern.text: For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.

original.text: καρδίᾳ γὰρ πιστεύεται εἰς δικαιοσύνην, στόματι δὲ ὁμολογεῖται εἰς σωτηρίαν·

verses.restored: For the Scripture says, Everyone trusting upon him will not be put to shame.

familiar.text: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

modern.text: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

original.text: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπʼ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.

verses.restored: For there is no distinction between Judean and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him.

familiar.text: For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him.

modern.text: For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him,

original.text: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολὴ Ἰουδαίου τε καὶ Ἕλληνος, ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων, πλουτῶν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους αὐτόν·

verses.restored: For everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved/healed.

familiar.text: For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

modern.text: for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”

original.text: Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.

verses.restored: How then may they call upon one in whom they did not trust? And how may they trust one whom they did not hear? And how may they hear without one announcing?

familiar.text: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?

modern.text: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?

original.text: Πῶς οὖν ⸀ἐπικαλέσωνται εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν; πῶς δὲ ⸀πιστεύσωσιν οὗ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; πῶς δὲ ⸀ἀκούσωσιν χωρὶς κηρύσσοντος;

verses.restored: And how may they announce unless they are sent? Just as it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those announcing good things.

familiar.text: And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

modern.text: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”

original.text: πῶς δὲ ⸀κηρύξωσιν ἐὰν μὴ ἀποσταλῶσιν; ⸀καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὡς ὡραῖοι οἱ πόδες τῶν ⸀εὐαγγελιζομένων ⸀τὰ ἀγαθά.

verses.restored: But not all obeyed the good news; for Isaiah says, Lord, who trusted our hearing-report?

familiar.text: But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?

modern.text: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”

original.text: ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντες ὑπήκουσαν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ· Ἠσαΐας γὰρ λέγει· Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν;

verses.restored: Therefore trust comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Messiah.

familiar.text: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

modern.text: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.

original.text: ἄρα ἡ πίστις ἐξ ἀκοῆς, ἡ δὲ ἀκοὴ διὰ ῥήματος ⸀Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: But I say, did they not hear? Indeed: Their voice went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.

familiar.text: But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.

modern.text: But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”

original.text: Ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ οὐκ ἤκουσαν; μενοῦνγε· Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν, καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But I say, did Israel not know? First Moses says, I will make you jealous by what is not a nation; by an uncomprehending nation I will provoke you.

familiar.text: But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you.

modern.text: I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says: “I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”

original.text: ἀλλὰ λέγω, μὴ ⸂Ἰσραὴλ οὐκ ἔγνω⸃; πρῶτος Μωϋσῆς λέγει· Ἐγὼ παραζηλώσω ὑμᾶς ἐπʼ οὐκ ἔθνει, ἐπʼ ἔθνει ἀσυνέτῳ παροργιῶ ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: And Isaiah is very bold and says, I was found by those not seeking me; I became manifest to those not asking for me.

familiar.text: But Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I was made manifest unto them that asked not after me.

modern.text: And Isaiah boldly says: “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”

original.text: Ἠσαΐας δὲ ἀποτολμᾷ καὶ λέγει· Εὑρέθην ⸀ἐν τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ζητοῦσιν, ἐμφανὴς ⸀ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἐμὲ μὴ ἐπερωτῶσιν.

verses.restored: But toward Israel he says, All day long I stretched out my hands toward a disobeying and contradicting people.

familiar.text: But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.

modern.text: But as for Israel he says: “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”

original.text: πρὸς δὲ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ λέγει· Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου πρὸς λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα.

safety_note: Romans 10 continues Paul's grief-filled argument for Israel and nations. It must not be detached as anti-Jewish triumphalism; Paul is arguing from Torah and Prophets as an Israelite, toward the mercy conclusion of Romans 11.
